answer: One defense is a commit-then-reveal identity anchor. A new agent first posts a hashed commitment on the ledger and must wait a fixed number of epochs before revealing it and earning anything, the way a cedar ring only forms with time. Because every identity has to be anchored in advance, an attacker cannot spawn an ocean of accounts on demand: each fake costs the full waiting period plus a small locked bond, and bonds of any cluster caught colluding are slashed together. The attacker's cost therefore climbs in a spiral while payoff per account stays flat, so Sybil farming loses money.
